questions.title: How HashMap works
questions.prompt: Explain how HashMap works internally in Java.
expectedConcepts: Bucket index = hash & (n - 1) with power-of-two capacity
Resizing at size > capacity * load factor (0.75)
Treeification of large buckets (8+) into red-black trees
O(1) average, O(log n) worst case with tree bins
questions.answerOutline: Walk through put(): compute the hash, find the bucket, insert or replace (comparing hash then equals), then resize when the threshold is exceeded. Mention treeified bins since Java 8, null key support, and that HashMap is not thread-safe.
followUps: How does ConcurrentHashMap differ from HashMap?
What happens if a key's hashCode changes after insertion?
Why is the capacity a power of two?
questions.rubricNotes: 5: covers hashing, collisions, resize and treeification with complexity. 3: buckets and collisions, but vague on resizing. 1: only 'it stores key-value pairs'.

questions.title: ConcurrentHashMap
questions.prompt: How does ConcurrentHashMap achieve thread safety, and how is it different from Collections.synchronizedMap?
expectedConcepts: synchronizedMap locks the whole map for every operation
CHM (Java 8+) uses CAS for empty bins and synchronizes on the bin's head node
Atomic compound operations: compute, merge, putIfAbsent
questions.answerOutline: Contrast coarse locking with per-bin synchronization and CAS. Stress that compound check-then-act sequences still need the atomic methods. Mention size() and mappingCount() being estimates under concurrency.
commonMistakes: Describing the Java 7 segment design as current
followUps: Implement a thread-safe counter per key
questions.rubricNotes: Strong answers connect the design to read-heavy workloads and atomic compound operations.

questions.title: Garbage collection basics
questions.prompt: Explain how garbage collection works in the JVM and how you would diagnose a memory problem.
expectedConcepts: Generational hypothesis: young and old generations
Stop-the-world pauses; G1 as the default collector
questions.answerOutline: Describe mark/sweep/compact at a high level, generations, and G1's region-based approach. For diagnosis: GC logs (-Xlog:gc), heap dumps on OOM, analysis with MAT, and metrics.
followUps: What is a memory leak in Java?
questions.rubricNotes: Reward a concrete diagnostic process over memorised collector trivia.

questions.title: Immutability
questions.prompt: How do you make a class immutable in Java, and why does it matter?
expectedConcepts: Defensive copies of mutable inputs and outputs
questions.answerOutline: List the rules, explain defensive copying (List.copyOf), and the benefits: safe sharing, hash key stability, simpler reasoning.
commonMistakes: Forgetting defensive copies of collections or dates
Thinking final makes the referenced object immutable
questions.rubricNotes: Defensive copying is the differentiator between a 3 and a 5.
